From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & capacity amendment: 8→16 GPU reserved pool (proposed terms)

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for taking time last week to review Novara's usage patterns. As we discussed, your current Dedicated reserved pool (8x A100-equivalent GPUs) will come up for renewal on Oct 15. Your usage profile over the past 3 months shows sustained growth during inference-heavy batches and nightly retrains; we're seeing consistent saturation windows that suggest an upgrade to 16 GPUs will meaningfully reduce queueing and tail latency for peak workloads.

High-level proposal (draft):
- New reserved pool: 16 GPUs (same region / dedicated tenancy)
- Term: 12 months starting on renewal date (Oct 15, 2027)
- Monthly commit: $78,000 / month (breakdown attached) — that reflects a blended per-GPU rate with predictability for burst capacity
- Throughput guardrail: baseline delivery target of 1.2M tokens/min aggregate across the pool during business hours; SLA addendum attached with details and remedies
- Ramp plan: 2-week canary (2→8 GPUs), 4-week full ramp to 16 with capacity verification and a roll-back path if any perf regressions are observed
- Autoscaling/burst: 20% burst headroom for short spikes (subject to scheduler policies).

Next steps I'd propose: I can send a formal amendment PDF that you can share with procurement and legal; Marissa (cc'd, CS lead) will coordinate the onboarding and the ramp runbook. If procurement needs Net30/PO terms call that out and we can work through finance.

Are you available Thursday (Sep 9) for a quick 20-min call to walk through the SLA addendum and price breakdown?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter

Appreciate the summary. A few quick questions for procurement/legal before we take that to the committee: 

1) Can you break the $78k/month into line items (base commit, burst buffer, monitoring/observability add-on)? I want a per-GPU delta to compare to our existing commit.
2) What is the guaranteed burst window (minutes) and how are overage charges handled if we exceed the 20% headroom?
3) For the SLA addendum: what remedies are you offering for repeated latency breaches (we've had two incidents in the last quarter that increased our P95 by ~230ms during peak jobs)?
4) Procurement typically requires Net30 and an invoice to match PO NB-2027-09. Any objections?

If it helps, please include the technical contact for the onboarding runbook (we'll need to align on canary windows with our infra team). I'm copying Jordan (procurement) and our contracts alias.

Ellen / Jordan —

Thanks — attached are the formal amendment and the SLA addendum you requested: Novara_Renewal_Amendment_v1.pdf and Throughput_SLA_Addendum.xlsx. I've also attached a simple CSV that shows the per-GPU blended unit price and the line-item split (cost-breakdown-8to16.csv). Short answers inline: 

1) Price split: base commit (16 GPUs) = $72,000 / month; observability & extended retention add-on = $4,500 / month; burst buffer reserve (short-window) = $1,500 / month. The per-GPU blended number on the amendment page 2 shows $4,500/GPU/month effective.

2) Burst window: default burst allowance is 20% for up to 15 minutes per hour (aggregated). If you exceed that, excess usage is billed at a reduced overage rate (0.6x of public on-demand) for the hours beyond allowance. We can also negotiate a larger burst buffer if Novara expects sustained spikes.

3) SLA remedies: the addendum defines a credit tiering model tied to P95 latency windows and availability; for repeated breaches we'll propose an operational review + incremental credits (detailed in sheet). For the two incidents you mentioned, we ran those traces internally and identified a scheduling contention during the nightly batch window; part of the upgrade plan includes a pinned GPU pool for batch jobs to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

4) Net30 / PO: Redwood can accept Net30 and invoice to PO NB-2027-09. Finance will require a signed amendment prior to the first invoice; we can prep DocuSign once terms are agreed.

Proposed next step: Marissa will own the ramp and runbook. If you confirm you want a revised amendment with Net30 and the 15% larger burst buffer (as an option), say so and I will circulate a v2.

Attachments: Novara_Renewal_Amendment_v1.pdf (amendment, pricing table), Throughput_SLA_Addendum.xlsx (SLA formulas and remedies), cost-breakdown-8to16.csv (per-GPU cost line items)

Cheers,
